summary: The proof is complete and correct. Positive normal rescaling preserves the cap halfspaces and exact affine-minorant structure assumed in the aligned subclass. On saturated fibers the barycentric cap computation gives the stated clipped quadratic loss, including thresholds 0 and 1/3. The three rescaled normals span the plane with their sole compatibility relation given by zero sum, so equation (21) defines one global affine map. Its fiberwise barycentric coordinates are computed correctly; the resulting constraints imply that the simplex-transportation product is at least 1/3 in every zero-, one-, and two-factor case. Shrinking the transported subtriangle produces the required mass-a_z/3 density with barycenter q(z). The lattice centerpoint and arbitrary-selected-mass nonempty-core theorem then apply with all hypotheses met and yield the factor-3 complete-core bound. Finally, each circuit cap belongs to the descendant collection, the partition into U, V, and B is exhaustive, and the loss estimates 3G, 5G, and 10a_z/9 combine exactly to give 3 eta W minus 8G, 5 eta W/3, and the mass bound 3 eta W/2. Degenerate set cases and all stated threshold boundaries are handled.
